owner_info.summary: Device name and short callsign visible to other users on the mesh.
owner_info.whenToUse: Change this when you need to label the device clearly or distinguish several of your nodes.
owner_info.defaultBehavior: If you leave it unchanged, the device keeps using the name already stored on the node.

fixed_position.summary: Manual device coordinates used when the device is stationary or GPS is not needed.
fixed_position.whenToUse: Set a fixed position for a home, rooftop, or other stationary node.
fixed_position.defaultBehavior: Without a manual position, the device usually uses GPS or sends no coordinates.

ringtone.summary: External notification melody in RTTTL format.
ringtone.whenToUse: Change it when you want a different sound for incoming notifications.
ringtone.defaultBehavior: If it is empty or unchanged, the device keeps the stored melody or firmware default.

device.summary: Core device behavior on the mesh: role, buttons, buzzer, and service announcements.
device.whenToUse: Open this section when choosing what the device is for: normal client, router, tracker, sensor, or TAK node.
device.defaultBehavior: For most users, the normal client role and defaults are appropriate.

position.summary: How the device gets and broadcasts its location.
position.whenToUse: Change these settings when you need to enable, limit, or tune position broadcasts.
position.defaultBehavior: Default values usually work for portable GPS devices.

power.summary: Sleep, wake, power saving, and power monitoring settings.
power.whenToUse: Use this for battery-powered devices, solar nodes, and any setup where runtime matters.
power.defaultBehavior: If the device has permanent power, the current values are usually fine.

network.summary: Wi-Fi, Ethernet, NTP, IP addresses, and network protocols on the device.
network.whenToUse: Change this when the device must join a local network, sync time, or send data over IP.
network.defaultBehavior: If networking is not used, leave these settings disabled or empty.

display.summary: Device screen behavior: screen timeout, coordinate format, orientation, units, and display mode.
display.whenToUse: Change this if the screen is hard to read, stays on too long, or needs a different coordinate format.
display.defaultBehavior: Default values usually work for the board's normal display.

lora.summary: LoRa radio settings: region, preset, power, frequency, hop limit, and packet filters.
lora.whenToUse: Change only if you understand the regional rules and need compatibility with a specific mesh.
lora.defaultBehavior: For non-expert users, keep the region and preset that already work in your network.
notes: Incorrect LoRa settings can make the node invisible to the rest of the mesh.

bluetooth.whenToUse: Change this when you need to allow or block Bluetooth access or set a fixed PIN.
bluetooth.defaultBehavior: Bluetooth is usually enabled when you configure the device from a phone or computer.

security.summary: Keys and administrative permissions that affect access to the device.
security.whenToUse: Change only if you manage network security or administrator access.
security.defaultBehavior: If you are not sure, do not change keys or administrative options.
notes: Wrong changes can lock you out of remote administration.

sessionkey.summary: Service section used to request a session key before administrative commands.
sessionkey.whenToUse: Usually does not require manual changes.

device_ui.summary: Built-in device UI: brightness, locks, language, node filters, map data, and screen notifications.
device_ui.whenToUse: Change this when the device has its own screen and controls.
device_ui.defaultBehavior: If the built-in UI is not used, most values can stay unchanged.

mqtt.summary: MQTT gateway for exchanging messages through the internet or a local broker.
mqtt.whenToUse: Enable it when you want to bridge the mesh to MQTT, a map, or external systems.
mqtt.defaultBehavior: If MQTT is not needed, leave the module disabled.

serial.summary: Serial module for data exchange through UART or the Serial API.
serial.whenToUse: Use it when the device is connected to another controller, computer, or external system over serial.
serial.defaultBehavior: If no external serial hardware is connected, the module is usually not needed.

external_notification.summary: External notifications: GPIO, vibration, buzzer, and reactions to messages or bell alerts.
external_notification.whenToUse: Configure this for external LEDs, vibration motors, buzzers, and other indicators.
external_notification.defaultBehavior: If no external notification hardware is connected, leave the module disabled.

store_forward.summary: Store & Forward stores messages and can return history to other nodes.
store_forward.whenToUse: Useful for stationary nodes that should help the mesh deliver message history.
store_forward.defaultBehavior: Usually not required for a normal portable device.

range_test.summary: Range Test sends test packets to measure coverage.
range_test.whenToUse: Enable temporarily while checking connectivity between locations.
range_test.defaultBehavior: Turn it off after testing to avoid unnecessary airtime.

telemetry.summary: Device, power, environment, health, and air quality telemetry.
telemetry.whenToUse: Enable only the telemetry types you need for connected sensors or power monitoring.
telemetry.defaultBehavior: Frequent telemetry uses more airtime and power.

canned_message.summary: Canned messages and hardware input controls for sending text from the device.
canned_message.whenToUse: Use it when the device has buttons or a rotary encoder for predefined messages.
canned_message.defaultBehavior: If those controls are not used, leave this section unchanged.

audio.summary: Codec2 audio module: PTT, bitrate, and I2S pins.
audio.whenToUse: Change only when compatible audio hardware is connected.
audio.defaultBehavior: Without audio hardware, the module is usually disabled.

remote_hardware.summary: Remote access to device GPIO pins through mesh commands.
remote_hardware.whenToUse: Use this for relays, sensors, and external automation.
remote_hardware.defaultBehavior: If remote automation is not needed, leave it disabled.

neighbor_info.summary: Information about nearby nodes that the device can report periodically.
neighbor_info.whenToUse: Useful for understanding mesh topology and which nodes can hear each other.
neighbor_info.defaultBehavior: Very frequent reports use airtime, so intervals are usually long.

ambient_lighting.summary: External RGB lighting: state, current, and colors.
ambient_lighting.whenToUse: Change only when supported lighting hardware is connected.
ambient_lighting.defaultBehavior: If no lighting is connected, leave it disabled.

detection_sensor.summary: GPIO event sensor, such as a button, reed switch, or motion sensor.
detection_sensor.whenToUse: Configure this when the device should send a message on input changes.
detection_sensor.defaultBehavior: A wrong trigger type may send too many messages or none at all.

paxcounter.summary: Counts nearby Wi-Fi/BLE devices using RSSI thresholds.
paxcounter.whenToUse: Use this for nearby presence estimation only where rules and laws allow it.
paxcounter.defaultBehavior: If this statistic is not needed, leave the module disabled.

statusmessage.summary: Text status that the node can rebroadcast periodically.
statusmessage.whenToUse: Set a short status when a stationary node should advertise its purpose or state.
statusmessage.defaultBehavior: An empty status avoids extra traffic.

traffic_management.summary: Mesh traffic optimization: deduplication, rate limiting, and unknown-packet handling.
traffic_management.whenToUse: Use in busy meshes or on infrastructure nodes.
traffic_management.defaultBehavior: If the mesh works normally, avoid changing this without understanding the effects.

tak.summary: TAK team and member role for TAK_TRACKER.

meshcore_device.summary: MeshCore Companion device metadata. This section is read-only.
meshcore_device.whenToUse: Use it to check the name, model, firmware version, and device keys.
meshcore_device.defaultBehavior: These values are reported by the device and are not edited from MeshApp.

meshcore_radio.summary: MeshCore Companion radio parameters. This section is read-only.
meshcore_radio.whenToUse: Use it to check frequency, power, and LoRa settings.
meshcore_radio.defaultBehavior: Values are reported by the device.

meshcore_limits.summary: MeshCore Companion limits, storage, and diagnostics.
meshcore_limits.whenToUse: Use it to understand available storage, contacts, channels, and the last error.
meshcore_limits.defaultBehavior: Values are reported by the device.

meshcore_channels.summary: MeshCore Companion channels and their roles. This section is read-only.
meshcore_channels.whenToUse: Use it to inspect configured channels.
meshcore_channels.defaultBehavior: Values are reported by the device.

owner_info.long_name.summary: Full device name. Use a human-readable label, such as Home Roof or Car 1.
owner_info.long_name.whenToUse: Change it when the device is hard to distinguish from other nodes.
owner_info.long_name.defaultBehavior: If unchanged, other users keep seeing the previous name.
owner_info.long_name.valueHint: Plain text. A short clear name works best.

owner_info.short_name.summary: Short device name used on screens and compact lists.
owner_info.short_name.whenToUse: Change it together with the long name so the node is recognizable in short form.
owner_info.short_name.defaultBehavior: If empty, the firmware or app may keep the existing short name.

owner_info.is_licensed.summary: Marks the owner as a licensed radio operator for regions or modes where radio rules allow different limits for licensed users.
owner_info.is_licensed.whenToUse: Enable only when the operator really has the required license or authorization for the region and band being used.
owner_info.is_licensed.defaultBehavior: If unsure, leave it disabled. In related owner information, the long name may need to contain the license number.
owner_info.is_licensed.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

true.title: Yes
true.description: The device marks the operator as licensed.

fixed_position.latitude.summary: Latitude of the device's fixed position.
fixed_position.latitude.whenToUse: Set it for a stationary node when you want to show its position without GPS.
fixed_position.latitude.defaultBehavior: A zero or empty value is not a useful coordinate.

fixed_position.longitude.summary: Longitude of the device's fixed position.
fixed_position.longitude.whenToUse: Set it together with latitude for a stationary node.
fixed_position.longitude.defaultBehavior: A zero or empty value is not a useful coordinate.

fixed_position.altitude.summary: Altitude of the fixed position above sea level.
fixed_position.altitude.whenToUse: Useful for rooftop and other high-mounted nodes.
fixed_position.altitude.defaultBehavior: If the exact altitude is unknown, keep the current value.

ringtone.ringtone.whenToUse: Change it when you want a custom external notification sound.
ringtone.ringtone.defaultBehavior: An empty string or current value keeps the default behavior.
ringtone.ringtone.valueHint: RTTTL text. If the format is invalid, the device may not play the melody.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.role.summary: Role defines why the device is on the mesh and how it handles other packets, position reports, and service messages.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.role.whenToUse: Change role only when the device's purpose changes: portable node, router, tracker, sensor, or TAK device.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.role.defaultBehavior: For most users, CLIENT is the correct choice. A wrong role can drain battery, use extra airtime, or make the node less visible.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.role.valueHint: Choose one value. If unsure, use CLIENT.

CLIENT.title: Normal node
CLIENT.description: Best for a phone, computer, or standalone messaging device. Recommended for most users.

CLIENT_MUTE.title: Client without rebroadcasting
CLIENT_MUTE.description: Participates in the mesh but does not forward other packets. Useful when you want less airtime usage.

ROUTER.title: Infrastructure router
ROUTER.description: Stationary coverage extender. Usually placed high and powered continuously.

ROUTER_CLIENT.title: Router-client
ROUTER_CLIENT.description: Deprecated mixed mode. Prefer ROUTER or CLIENT.

REPEATER.title: Simple repeater
REPEATER.description: Deprecated mode that only repeats packets and can create routing problems.

TRACKER.title: Tracker
TRACKER.description: Sends position more often. Good for moving objects, but uses more power and airtime.

SENSOR.title: Sensor
SENSOR.description: Prioritizes telemetry. Use for weather, environment, and other sensor nodes.

TAK.title: TAK
TAK.description: Mode for ATAK integration. Not needed for normal messaging.

CLIENT_HIDDEN.title: Hidden client
CLIENT_HIDDEN.description: Sends fewer routine announcements while still allowing on-demand communication. Use only if you understand the tradeoff.

LOST_AND_FOUND.title: Lost and found
LOST_AND_FOUND.description: Regularly sends a text message with current position to help recover the device.

TAK_TRACKER.title: TAK tracker
TAK_TRACKER.description: Automatically sends position for TAK and reduces routine announcements.

ROUTER_LATE.title: Late router
ROUTER_LATE.description: Rebroadcasts after other routers. Useful as backup coverage without competing with main routers.

CLIENT_BASE.title: Base client
CLIENT_BASE.description: Helps weaker favorite nodes distribute messages more widely. Good for a home or rooftop base station.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.serial_en.summary: Legacy device option that used to enable the Serial Console over the Stream API. New firmware uses Security > Serial enabled, so this field is kept mainly for older configurations.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.serial_en.whenToUse: Change only when managing an old firmware/configuration that still reads this Device field.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.serial_en.defaultBehavior: For current firmware, configure the Security section instead and leave this legacy value unchanged.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.serial_en.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.button_gp.summary: GPIO pin used as the user button on boards without a predefined button, or to remap the button function on boards with multiple buttons.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.button_gp.whenToUse: Set it when your board documentation says the user button should be on a specific GPIO, or when you intentionally move that function to another button.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.button_gp.defaultBehavior: Boards with a built-in button normally already know the correct pin. Keep the default unless you are wiring your own button.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.button_gp.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_gp.summary: GPIO pin used to drive a PWM buzzer on boards without a predefined buzzer pin.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_gp.whenToUse: Set it when you have connected an external buzzer or your board needs a custom buzzer pin.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_gp.defaultBehavior: Boards with a built-in buzzer normally use their predefined pin. Keep the default unless your hardware wiring is different.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_gp.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.rebroadca.summary: Controls which packets this node is allowed to rebroadcast for other nodes. It affects network reach, airtime use, and whether foreign or unknown traffic is forwarded.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.rebroadca.whenToUse: Change it when you need to reduce airtime, limit forwarding to your own mesh, or configure a tracker/sensor that should not relay packets.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.rebroadca.defaultBehavior: For normal client nodes, ALL is the usual default. Restrictive modes can reduce mesh coverage if chosen incorrectly.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.rebroadca.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

ALL.title: All
ALL.description: Rebroadcasts normal mesh traffic broadly, including compatible traffic from other meshes with the same radio parameters.

ALL_SKIP_DECODING.title: All, skip decoding
ALL_SKIP_DECODING.description: Repeats packets without decoding them. Intended for Repeater role; other roles fall back to ALL behavior.

LOCAL_ONLY.title: Local only
LOCAL_ONLY.description: Rebroadcasts only packets from local primary or secondary channels and ignores open or undecryptable foreign mesh traffic.

KNOWN_ONLY.title: Known only
KNOWN_ONLY.description: Like LOCAL_ONLY, but also ignores packets from node numbers that are not in this node database.

NONE.title: None
NONE.description: Does not rebroadcast packets. Allowed only for Sensor, Tracker, and TAK Tracker style roles.

CORE_PORTNUMS_ONLY.title: Core packets only
CORE_PORTNUMS_ONLY.description: Rebroadcasts standard Meshtastic packet types such as NodeInfo, Text, Position, Telemetry, and Routing, while ignoring non-standard portnums.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.node_info.summary: How often the node broadcasts its NodeInfo: long name, short name, and identity information that other devices show in node lists.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.node_info.whenToUse: Increase the interval to reduce airtime, or decrease it if nodes often appear unnamed or stale in your network.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.node_info.defaultBehavior: The firmware default is usually safe. Very frequent NodeInfo broadcasts add traffic without improving normal messaging.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.node_info.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.double_ta.summary: Treats a double tap from a supported accelerometer as if the user button was pressed.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.double_ta.whenToUse: Enable it when the device has a supported accelerometer and you want tap control without pressing a physical button.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.double_ta.defaultBehavior: Leave disabled if the device has no accelerometer or accidental taps would be inconvenient.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.double_ta.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.is_manage.summary: Legacy flag that marked the node as managed by a mesh administrator and limited what normal users could change in clients.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.is_manage.whenToUse: Use the Security section for current firmware. This old Device field is useful only for compatibility with old configs.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.is_manage.defaultBehavior: Leave disabled unless an administrator intentionally manages the node and the firmware still uses this legacy field.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.is_manage.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.disable_t.summary: Disables the user-button triple-click shortcut that toggles GPS on or off.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.disable_t.whenToUse: Enable this if accidental triple-clicks are turning GPS off, or if the button is used for another enclosure-specific action.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.disable_t.defaultBehavior: Leave disabled when you want the quick GPS toggle to remain available from the device button.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.disable_t.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.tzdef.summary: POSIX timezone string used by the device to show local time on its screen and in logs.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.tzdef.whenToUse: Set it when the displayed time is wrong or the device needs a timezone without relying on a connected phone.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.tzdef.defaultBehavior: UTC0 is safe for UTC. For local time, use a valid POSIX timezone string for your region.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.tzdef.valueHint: Enter a POSIX TZ string, for example UTC0 or a region-specific rule such as PST8PDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.led_heart.summary: Turns off the default blinking status LED heartbeat.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.led_heart.whenToUse: Enable it if the blinking LED is distracting, wastes power, or must stay dark in your installation.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.led_heart.defaultBehavior: Leave disabled if you want the LED to keep showing that the device is alive.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.led_heart.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_mo.summary: Controls which sounds the device buzzer is allowed to play: all feedback, no sound, only notifications, only system tones, or only direct-message alerts.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_mo.whenToUse: Change it to make the device quieter, keep only important alerts, or disable button/startup sounds while still allowing notifications.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_mo.defaultBehavior: ALL_ENABLED gives full audible feedback. DISABLED makes the device silent, which can cause missed alerts.
meshtastic.Config.DeviceConfig.buzzer_mo.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

ALL_ENABLED.title: All sounds
ALL_ENABLED.description: Buzzer plays all audio feedback: button presses, startup/shutdown tones, notifications, and alerts.

DISABLED.title: Silent
DISABLED.description: All buzzer feedback is disabled. Use when the device must not make sound.

NOTIFICATIONS_ONLY.title: Notifications only
NOTIFICATIONS_ONLY.description: Buzzer plays notifications and alerts, but not button-press or routine system tones.

SYSTEM_ONLY.title: System sounds only
SYSTEM_ONLY.description: Buzzer plays non-notification tones such as button presses, startup, and shutdown, but not message alerts.

DIRECT_MSG_ONLY.title: Direct messages only
DIRECT_MSG_ONLY.description: Buzzer plays direct-message notifications and alerts, but not button-press sounds.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.summary: position broadcast secs controls how often Position sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls GPS, fixed location, and how often position packets are sent.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.summary: Enables adaptive position broadcasting. The node sends position updates when movement and timing make the update useful instead of blindly sending on every interval.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.whenToUse: Keep enabled for most mobile devices to reduce radio traffic and battery use while still updating the map when the node moves.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.defaultBehavior: Disabling it makes position broadcasts follow the regular interval more directly and can increase airtime.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.fixed_p.summary: Marks the node as stationary. The device keeps sending the configured last latitude, longitude, and altitude instead of requiring a fresh GPS fix.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.fixed_p.whenToUse: Use for a base station, repeater, router, or indoor node that has a known permanent location and no useful GPS reception.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.fixed_p.defaultBehavior: Wrong fixed coordinates will put the node in the wrong place on maps and can mislead other users.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.fixed_p.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_ena.summary: Deprecated GPS on/off flag. New firmware uses GPS mode to say whether GPS is enabled, disabled, or not present on the device.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_ena.whenToUse: Change only for old firmware that still reads this field. For current firmware, use GPS mode.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_ena.defaultBehavior: Leave unchanged if GPS mode is available.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_ena.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_upd.summary: gps update interval controls how often Position sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls GPS, fixed location, and how often position packets are sent.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_upd.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_upd.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_upd.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_att.summary: Deprecated limit for how long the device tries to obtain a GPS position. Newer firmware relies on smart and regular broadcast timing instead.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_att.whenToUse: Use only with old firmware or when diagnosing GPS startup behavior on a specific device.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_att.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.summary: Bit mask that chooses which extra details are included in POSITION packets, such as altitude, satellite count, timestamp, heading, and speed.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.whenToUse: Enable extra fields only when receivers need them. More fields make every position packet larger and increase airtime.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.defaultBehavior: The firmware always includes core coordinates; optional fields should stay minimal on busy meshes.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.positio.valueHint: This is a bit mask. Use dedicated UI controls if available; otherwise change it only when you know which flags are being combined.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.rx_gpio.summary: rx gpio selects the hardware line used by Position. This section controls GPS, fixed location, and how often position packets are sent.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.rx_gpio.whenToUse: Set it according to your board or external module wiring.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.rx_gpio.defaultBehavior: Board defaults are safest for built-in hardware; wrong pins can stop the feature or conflict with another function.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.rx_gpio.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.tx_gpio.summary: tx gpio selects the hardware line used by Position. This section controls GPS, fixed location, and how often position packets are sent.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.tx_gpio.whenToUse: Set it according to your board or external module wiring.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.tx_gpio.defaultBehavior: Board defaults are safest for built-in hardware; wrong pins can stop the feature or conflict with another function.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.tx_gpio.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.summary: Minimum movement in meters before smart position broadcasting is allowed to send another location update.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce map updates and save airtime; decrease it when nearby movement must appear quickly.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.defaultBehavior: Too small a distance can flood the mesh with position packets; too large a distance makes moving nodes look stale.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.summary: broadcast smart minimum interval secs controls how often Position sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls GPS, fixed location, and how often position packets are sent.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.broadca.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_en_.summary: gps en gpio selects the hardware line used by Position. This section controls GPS, fixed location, and how often position packets are sent.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_en_.whenToUse: Set it according to your board or external module wiring.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_en_.defaultBehavior: Board defaults are safest for built-in hardware; wrong pins can stop the feature or conflict with another function.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_en_.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_mod.summary: Tells firmware whether GPS hardware is present and should be used.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_mod.whenToUse: Use ENABLED when the node has GPS and should report movement, DISABLED when GPS exists but should stay off, and NOT_PRESENT when no GPS hardware is installed.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_mod.defaultBehavior: Wrong mode can waste power or prevent positions from updating.
meshtastic.Config.PositionConfig.gps_mod.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

DISABLED.title: Disabled
DISABLED.description: GPS hardware exists but firmware should not use it.

ENABLED.title: Enabled
ENABLED.description: GPS hardware exists and should provide live position data.

NOT_PRESENT.title: Not present
NOT_PRESENT.description: The device has no GPS hardware; firmware will not wait for GPS fixes.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.is_power_s.summary: Lets the device sleep as much as possible. For tracker and sensor roles this can also sleep the LoRa radio between activity periods.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.is_power_s.whenToUse: Use for battery-powered trackers and sensors that do not need constant phone connection or instant responses.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.is_power_s.defaultBehavior: Do not use when you need reliable phone app access, quick interaction, or a device without a user button to wake it.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.is_power_s.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.on_battery.summary: on battery shutdown after secs controls how often Power sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls sleep, wake-up, and battery behavior.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.on_battery.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.on_battery.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.on_battery.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.adc_multip.summary: Overrides the battery-voltage divider ratio used to calculate displayed battery voltage.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.adc_multip.whenToUse: Use only when the board reports the wrong battery voltage and you know the resistor divider ratio for that hardware.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.adc_multip.defaultBehavior: Leave empty/default on normal boards. A wrong multiplier makes battery percentage and voltage readings unreliable.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.adc_multip.valueHint: Enter a decimal ratio, usually between 2 and 6.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.wait_bluet.summary: wait bluetooth secs controls how often Power sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls sleep, wake-up, and battery behavior.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.wait_bluet.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.wait_bluet.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.wait_bluet.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.sds_secs.summary: sds secs controls how often Power sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls sleep, wake-up, and battery behavior.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.sds_secs.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.sds_secs.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.sds_secs.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.ls_secs.summary: ls secs controls how often Power sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls sleep, wake-up, and battery behavior.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.ls_secs.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.ls_secs.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.ls_secs.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.min_wake_s.summary: min wake secs controls how often Power sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls sleep, wake-up, and battery behavior.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.min_wake_s.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.min_wake_s.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.min_wake_s.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.device_bat.summary: device battery ina address is a connection value used by Power. This section controls sleep, wake-up, and battery behavior.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.device_bat.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.device_bat.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.device_bat.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.powermon_e.summary: Debug bit mask for enabling selected power-monitor log sources.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.powermon_e.whenToUse: Use while diagnosing power consumption or sleep behavior with logs. It is not needed for normal operation.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.powermon_e.defaultBehavior: Leave 0/empty unless you are collecting power diagnostics.
meshtastic.Config.PowerConfig.powermon_e.valueHint: This is a bit mask. Enable only the log sources you need.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ena.summary: Enables Wi-Fi on the node. On supported devices, enabling Wi-Fi disables Bluetooth because the radios share resources.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ena.whenToUse: Use when the node must connect to a Wi-Fi network for MQTT, NTP time sync, syslog, or other network services.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ena.defaultBehavior: Keep disabled if you normally connect from the phone over Bluetooth.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ena.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ssi.summary: wifi ssid is a connection value used by Network. This section controls Wi-Fi, Ethernet, time sync, IP address, and network services.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ssi.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ssi.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_ssi.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_psk.summary: wifi psk is a connection value used by Network. This section controls Wi-Fi, Ethernet, time sync, IP address, and network services.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_psk.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_psk.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.wifi_psk.valueHint: Enter the value exactly; an extra space or wrong character can prevent access.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ntp_serv.summary: ntp server is a connection value used by Network. This section controls Wi-Fi, Ethernet, time sync, IP address, and network services.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ntp_serv.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ntp_serv.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ntp_serv.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.eth_enab.summary: Enables Ethernet networking on boards that have supported Ethernet hardware.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.eth_enab.whenToUse: Use for fixed nodes where a wired connection is more reliable than Wi-Fi.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.eth_enab.defaultBehavior: Leave disabled on boards without Ethernet or when using Wi-Fi/Bluetooth only.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.eth_enab.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.address_.summary: Chooses how the node gets its IP address: DHCP automatically from the router, or STATIC from values you enter manually.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.address_.whenToUse: Use DHCP for ordinary home or field networks. Use STATIC only when the network administrator expects the node to keep a fixed IP address.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.address_.defaultBehavior: A wrong static IP, gateway, subnet, or DNS can make the node unreachable on the network.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.address_.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

DHCP.title: DHCP
DHCP.description: Router gives the node IP address, gateway, subnet, and DNS automatically.

STATIC.title: Static
STATIC.description: You manually enter IP address, gateway, subnet, and DNS. Use when your network requires a fixed address.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv4_con.summary: Parameter group "ipv4 config" in the "network" section. It contains related settings.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv4_con.whenToUse: Open this group when you need to change the related "ipv4 config" settings.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv4_con.defaultBehavior: If you are not sure, keep the current value. A wrong setting can reduce connectivity, drain battery, or disable a needed feature.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv4_con.valueHint: Enter text without extra spaces. For addresses, keys, and formats, use the exact value.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.summary: Static IPv4 address assigned to this node when Address mode is STATIC.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.whenToUse: Set when the router or network plan requires this node to keep a fixed address.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.defaultBehavior: Do not fill for DHCP. Duplicate or wrong IP addresses cause network conflicts.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.valueHint: Use a valid IPv4 address for your LAN, for example 192.168.1.50.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.summary: IPv4 address of the router/gateway used when Address mode is STATIC.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.whenToUse: Set with the static IP so the node can reach devices outside its local subnet.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.defaultBehavior: Wrong gateway can leave Wi-Fi/Ethernet connected but prevent internet, MQTT, or NTP access.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.valueHint: Use your router address, for example 192.168.1.1.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.summary: Subnet mask for the static IPv4 network.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.whenToUse: Set together with static IP and gateway according to your LAN addressing plan.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.defaultBehavior: Wrong subnet can stop the node from reaching nearby devices even when the IP address looks correct.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.valueHint: Common home networks use 255.255.255.0, but follow your network settings.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.summary: DNS server used to resolve names such as MQTT or NTP hosts when Address mode is STATIC.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.whenToUse: Set when using host names instead of raw IP addresses with a static network configuration.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.defaultBehavior: Wrong DNS can break named servers while direct IP addresses still work.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.IpV4Conf.valueHint: Use your router DNS or a DNS server allowed by your network.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.rsyslog_.summary: rsyslog server is a connection value used by Network. This section controls Wi-Fi, Ethernet, time sync, IP address, and network services.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.rsyslog_.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.rsyslog_.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.rsyslog_.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.enabled_.summary: Bit mask for optional network protocols, such as UDP broadcast on the local network.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.enabled_.whenToUse: Enable only the protocols you actually need for local discovery or integration.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.enabled_.defaultBehavior: Leaving optional broadcasts off reduces unnecessary LAN traffic.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.enabled_.valueHint: 0 means no auxiliary broadcast. UDP_BROADCAST enables local UDP packet broadcasting.

meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv6_ena.summary: Enables IPv6 support for network features when the firmware and local network support it.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv6_ena.whenToUse: Use only on networks where IPv6 is configured and needed.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv6_ena.defaultBehavior: IPv4 is enough for most simple Wi-Fi and Ethernet setups.
meshtastic.Config.NetworkConfig.ipv6_ena.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.screen_o.summary: screen on secs controls how often Display sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls the built-in screen and how information is shown on it.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.screen_o.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.screen_o.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.screen_o.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.gps_form.summary: Deprecated, unused display GPS format field. New firmware no longer uses this setting.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.gps_form.whenToUse: Do not change it for current firmware; use the active GPS format setting in Device UI where available.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.gps_form.defaultBehavior: Leave unchanged because this field is kept only for compatibility.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.gps_form.valueHint: No useful value is expected for current firmware.

UNUSED.title: Unused
UNUSED.description: Deprecated value kept only for compatibility.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.auto_scr.summary: auto screen carousel secs controls how often Display sends, updates, or repeats its data. This section controls the built-in screen and how information is shown on it.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.auto_scr.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.auto_scr.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.auto_scr.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.summary: Deprecated display option that kept north at the top of the compass instead of rotating the display toward the current heading.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.whenToUse: Use only on old firmware or old display layouts that still support this behavior.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.defaultBehavior: Leave unchanged on current firmware unless you are correcting a known compass display issue.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.flip_scr.summary: Flips the built-in screen vertically for devices mounted upside down.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.flip_scr.whenToUse: Use when the physical device or case forces the screen to be installed inverted.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.flip_scr.defaultBehavior: Leave off when text and icons already appear upright.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.flip_scr.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.units.summary: Chooses metric or imperial units for values shown on the device screen.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.units.whenToUse: Set to the units your users expect for distance, speed, altitude, and similar display values.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.units.defaultBehavior: Metric is the normal default in firmware.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.units.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

METRIC.title: Metric
METRIC.description: Shows distances and measurements in metric units.

IMPERIAL.title: Imperial
IMPERIAL.description: Shows distances and measurements in imperial units.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.oled.summary: Selects the OLED display driver/type when automatic detection fails.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.oled.whenToUse: Use only when the screen is blank, wrong size, or drawn incorrectly and you know the display controller installed on the board.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.oled.defaultBehavior: AUTO should be used for most devices.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.oled.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

OLED_AUTO.title: Auto detect
OLED_AUTO.description: Firmware tries to detect the screen automatically.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.displaym.summary: Chooses the layout style used on the device display, including layouts for classic OLED and bicolor screens.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.displaym.whenToUse: Change when the default layout wastes space, looks wrong on a bicolor display, or needs an inverted top bar.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.displaym.defaultBehavior: Default layout is safest for ordinary 128x64 OLED screens.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.displaym.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

TWOCOLOR.title: Two-color
TWOCOLOR.description: Layout adjusted for bicolor OLED screens.

INVERTED.title: Inverted
INVERTED.description: Two-color style with inverted top bar.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.heading_.summary: Makes the first line on the device display use a pseudo-bold style.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.heading_.whenToUse: Use when the top line is hard to read at a glance.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.heading_.defaultBehavior: Leave off for the original lighter display style.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.heading_.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.wake_on_.summary: Wakes the screen when a supported accelerometer detects a tap or movement.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.wake_on_.whenToUse: Use on handheld devices where users expect the screen to wake without pressing the button.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.wake_on_.defaultBehavior: Leave off if motion wakes the screen too often and wastes battery.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.wake_on_.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.summary: Rotates or inverts compass readings so the on-screen compass matches the way the hardware is mounted.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.whenToUse: Change after installing the device in a case or mount where the compass direction is consistently rotated or reversed.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.defaultBehavior: Use 0 degrees when the compass and display are mounted in the same orientation.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.compass_.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

DEGREES_0.description: Compass output is rotated by 0 degrees.

DEGREES_0_INVERTED.title: 0° inverted
DEGREES_0_INVERTED.description: Compass output is rotated by 0 degrees and inverted.

DEGREES_90.description: Compass output is rotated by 90 degrees.

DEGREES_90_INVERTED.title: 90° inverted
DEGREES_90_INVERTED.description: Compass output is rotated by 90 degrees and inverted.

DEGREES_180.description: Compass output is rotated by 180 degrees.

DEGREES_180_INVERTED.title: 180° inverted
DEGREES_180_INVERTED.description: Compass output is rotated by 180 degrees and inverted.

DEGREES_270.description: Compass output is rotated by 270 degrees.

DEGREES_270_INVERTED.title: 270° inverted
DEGREES_270_INVERTED.description: Compass output is rotated by 270 degrees and inverted.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_12h_.summary: Chooses 12-hour clock display instead of the default 24-hour format on the device screen.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_12h_.whenToUse: Use when users prefer AM/PM time format.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_12h_.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_long.summary: Shows long node names on device screens instead of short names where the UI supports it.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_long.whenToUse: Use when short names are ambiguous and the screen has enough room.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_long.defaultBehavior: Short names are easier to read on small OLED displays.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.use_long.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.enable_m.summary: Shows received messages as bubbles on the device screen.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.enable_m.whenToUse: Use on devices with screens when local users need to read messages without opening the phone app.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.enable_m.defaultBehavior: Disable if message bubbles clutter the screen or reveal messages in a shared space.
meshtastic.Config.DisplayConfig.enable_m.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.Config.LoRaConfig.use_preset.summary: Use a predefined Meshtastic modem preset instead of manual bandwidth, spreading factor, and coding rate. These radio settings determine whether nodes can hear each other and whether operation is legal for the region.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_filter.summary: Saved node-list filter configuration used by the on-device UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_filter.whenToUse: Use when the device screen should hide nodes that are offline, unknown, distant, or not relevant.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_filter.defaultBehavior: Restrictive filters can make valid nodes disappear from the local screen.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_filter.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.unknown_switch.summary: Hides nodes whose details are still unknown in the on-device node list.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.unknown_switch.whenToUse: Use to keep the list cleaner when many incomplete or newly heard nodes appear.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.unknown_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable if you want to see every node the device has heard.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.unknown_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.offline_switch.summary: Hides nodes that are currently considered offline from the on-device node list.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.offline_switch.whenToUse: Use when the list is crowded and users mostly need active nodes.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.offline_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable if offline nodes are still important for history or diagnostics.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.offline_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.public_key_switch.summary: Hides nodes that do not have a public key recorded.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.public_key_switch.whenToUse: Use when users only want nodes that can participate in secure identity/key features.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.public_key_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable to show older or incomplete node records too.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.public_key_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.hops_away.summary: Filters the node list by mesh distance in hops.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.hops_away.whenToUse: Use to focus the on-device list on nearby nodes or to hide nodes that are many relays away.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.hops_away.defaultBehavior: A restrictive hop filter can make valid distant nodes disappear from the display.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.hops_away.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.position_switch.summary: Hides nodes that do not have a known position.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.position_switch.whenToUse: Use when the display is being used mainly for map/location awareness.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.position_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable if non-GPS nodes should still appear.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.position_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.node_name.summary: Filters the node list by a matching name string.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.node_name.whenToUse: Use to show only nodes whose long or short name contains the text you enter.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.node_name.defaultBehavior: Empty text means no name filter.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.node_name.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.NodeFilter.channel.summary: Filters the node list by channel index.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.channel.whenToUse: Use when the device participates in several channels and users need to focus one channel.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.channel.defaultBehavior: Wrong channel filter can hide nodes that are still present on other channels.
meshtastic.NodeFilter.channel.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_highlight.summary: Saved node-list highlight rules used by the on-device UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_highlight.whenToUse: Use when important nodes should stand out by chat, position, telemetry, IAQ, or name.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_highlight.defaultBehavior: Highlighting changes display priority only; it does not change mesh traffic.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.node_highlight.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.NodeHighlight.chat_switch.summary: Highlights nodes with active chat activity in the on-device list.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.chat_switch.whenToUse: Use when recent conversations should stand out from ordinary nodes.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.chat_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable for a plainer node list.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.chat_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeHighlight.position_switch.summary: Highlights nodes that have position information.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.position_switch.whenToUse: Use when location-capable nodes should be easy to spot.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.position_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable if position should not affect visual priority.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.position_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeHighlight.telemetry_switc.summary: Highlights nodes that provide telemetry data.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.telemetry_switc.whenToUse: Use when sensor or device-status nodes should stand out.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.telemetry_switc.defaultBehavior: Disable if telemetry should not affect the list appearance.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.telemetry_switc.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeHighlight.iaq_switch.whenToUse: Use when air quality sensors should be easy to find on the device.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.iaq_switch.defaultBehavior: Disable if IAQ data is not important for the current user.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.iaq_switch.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.NodeHighlight.node_name.summary: Highlights nodes whose name matches the entered text.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.node_name.whenToUse: Use to visually mark a team, site, or group of important nodes.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.node_name.defaultBehavior: Empty text means no name-based highlight.
meshtastic.NodeHighlight.node_name.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.calibration_da.summary: Touch or screen calibration bytes stored by the device UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.calibration_da.whenToUse: Use only when restoring calibration data for the same device/screen.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.calibration_da.defaultBehavior: Wrong calibration data can make touch input inaccurate.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.calibration_da.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.map_data.summary: Saved map settings for the on-device UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.map_data.whenToUse: Use to keep home location, map style, and follow-GPS behavior for devices with map UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.map_data.defaultBehavior: Wrong map data changes only local display behavior.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.map_data.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.Map.home.summary: Parameter group "home" in the "device screen UI" section. It contains related settings.
meshtastic.Map.home.whenToUse: Open this group when you need to change the related "home" settings.
meshtastic.Map.home.defaultBehavior: If you are not sure, keep the current value. A wrong setting can reduce connectivity, drain battery, or disable a needed feature.
meshtastic.Map.home.valueHint: Enter text without extra spaces. For addresses, keys, and formats, use the exact value.

meshtastic.GeoPoint.zoom.summary: Zoom level for the saved map point used by the device UI.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.zoom.whenToUse: Increase to show a closer map view around the point; decrease to show a wider area.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.zoom.defaultBehavior: Wrong zoom affects only the local map view, not radio or GPS operation.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.zoom.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.GeoPoint.latitude.summary: Latitude of the saved map point, usually the home point for the device UI map.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.latitude.whenToUse: Set when you want the on-device map to open around a known home or base location.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.latitude.defaultBehavior: Wrong latitude moves the displayed home point to the wrong place.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.latitude.valueHint: Use the coordinate format expected by this UI data. If the value was written by the device, keep the same format.

meshtastic.GeoPoint.longitude.summary: Longitude of the saved map point, usually the home point for the device UI map.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.longitude.whenToUse: Set together with latitude when you want the on-device map to open around a known home or base location.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.longitude.defaultBehavior: Wrong longitude moves the displayed home point to the wrong place.
meshtastic.GeoPoint.longitude.valueHint: Use the coordinate format expected by this UI data. If the value was written by the device, keep the same format.

meshtastic.Map.style.summary: Map tile/style identifier used by the on-device map UI.
meshtastic.Map.style.whenToUse: Change when the device supports multiple map styles and users need a different visual map layer.
meshtastic.Map.style.defaultBehavior: Unsupported style names may fall back to default or show no map tiles.
meshtastic.Map.style.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.Map.follow_gps.summary: Makes the on-device map follow the current GPS position as the node moves.
meshtastic.Map.follow_gps.whenToUse: Use for handheld or vehicle devices where the user wants the map centered on the node.
meshtastic.Map.follow_gps.defaultBehavior: Disable when users need to pan around the map without it snapping back to GPS.
meshtastic.Map.follow_gps.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.compass_mode.summary: Chooses the visual compass behavior on the device UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.compass_mode.whenToUse: Use the mode that is easiest to read for the device mounting and use case.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.compass_mode.defaultBehavior: This affects display behavior, not the actual GPS or radio position.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.compass_mode.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic
DYNAMIC.description: Compass ring and heading move dynamically.

FIXED_RING.title: Fixed ring
FIXED_RING.description: Compass ring stays fixed while heading changes.

FREEZE_HEADING.title: Freeze heading
FREEZE_HEADING.description: Keeps a heading reference frozen for easier navigation.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.screen_rgb_col.summary: RGB accent color used by the BaseUI screen.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.screen_rgb_col.whenToUse: Use to personalize the device UI or make a deployed group visually distinct.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.screen_rgb_col.valueHint: Use 0xRRGGBB format, for example 0xFF0000 for red.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.is_clockface_a.summary: Chooses analog clockface instead of digital clockface on the device UI.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.is_clockface_a.whenToUse: Use when the user prefers an analog clock display.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.is_clockface_a.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.gps_format.summary: Chooses how GPS coordinates are printed on the device screen.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.gps_format.whenToUse: Use the coordinate format your users or external maps expect.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.gps_format.defaultBehavior: A different format changes display only; it does not change the actual location.
meshtastic.DeviceUIConfig.gps_format.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

DEC.title: Decimal degrees
DEC.description: Coordinates as decimal degrees, common for maps and apps.

DMS.title: Degrees minutes seconds
DMS.description: Coordinates as degrees, minutes, and seconds.

OLC.title: Plus Code
OLC.description: Open Location Code / Plus Code format.

OSGR.title: OS Grid
OSGR.description: United Kingdom Ordnance Survey grid reference.

MLS.title: Maidenhead
MLS.description: Maidenhead Locator System, common in amateur radio.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.enabl.summary: Turns MQTT on or off. MQTT bridges mesh traffic or map reports to an MQTT broker.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.enabl.whenToUse: Enable it only when you use mqtt; disable it to save resources and avoid extra traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.enabl.defaultBehavior: Disabled is safest when the feature is not installed or not needed.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.enabl.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.addre.summary: address is a connection value used by MQTT. MQTT bridges mesh traffic or map reports to an MQTT broker.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.addre.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.addre.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.addre.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.usern.summary: username is a connection value used by MQTT. MQTT bridges mesh traffic or map reports to an MQTT broker.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.usern.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.usern.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.usern.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.passw.summary: password is a connection value used by MQTT. MQTT bridges mesh traffic or map reports to an MQTT broker.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.passw.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.passw.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.passw.valueHint: Enter the value exactly; an extra space or wrong character can prevent access.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.encry.summary: Controls whether packets published to MQTT stay encrypted or may be sent decrypted for integrations.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.encry.whenToUse: Keep enabled for privacy. Disable only when a trusted external system must read message contents from MQTT.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.encry.defaultBehavior: Decrypted MQTT traffic can expose message content outside the radio mesh.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.encry.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.json_.summary: Deprecated MQTT JSON packet option. JSON packet support was removed and firmware ignores this field.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.json_.whenToUse: Do not use for new setups. It remains only so old configurations can still be read.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.json_.defaultBehavior: Changing it should not enable JSON MQTT output on current firmware.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.json_.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.tls_e.summary: Enables TLS for the MQTT connection, so the broker connection is encrypted in transit.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.tls_e.whenToUse: Use when connecting to an MQTT broker that supports or requires secure TLS connections.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.tls_e.defaultBehavior: Wrong TLS setting can prevent connection if the broker expects the opposite mode.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.tls_e.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.root.summary: root is a connection value used by MQTT. MQTT bridges mesh traffic or map reports to an MQTT broker.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.root.whenToUse: Change it when connecting the node to your own Wi-Fi, MQTT broker, NTP server, syslog server, or topic namespace.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.root.defaultBehavior: One wrong character can prevent connection. Keep empty/default values when using firmware defaults.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.root.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.proxy.summary: Allows a connected phone or client to proxy MQTT traffic for the node instead of the node connecting directly.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.proxy.whenToUse: Use when the node lacks its own Wi-Fi/Ethernet internet path but a connected client can reach MQTT.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.proxy.defaultBehavior: Disable when the node should only use its own network connection or should not depend on a client.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.proxy.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.summary: Periodically publishes unencrypted node information for map reporting through MQTT.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.whenToUse: Enable only when the user intentionally wants this node to appear in MQTT map/reporting systems.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.defaultBehavior: This can publish location or identifying information outside the local mesh, so leave off unless the user opts in.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.summary: Parameter group "map report settings" in the "MQTT" section. It contains related settings.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.whenToUse: Open this group when you need to change the related "map report settings" settings.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.defaultBehavior: If you are not sure, keep the current value. A wrong setting can reduce connectivity, drain battery, or disable a needed feature.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MQTTConfig.map_r.valueHint: Enter text without extra spaces. For addresses, keys, and formats, use the exact value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.summary: publish interval secs controls how often MQTT map reporting sends, updates, or repeats its data. Map reporting publishes selected node information through MQTT.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.summary: Location precision, in bits, used when reporting position to the MQTT map.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.whenToUse: Lower it to blur the published location for privacy; use full precision only when exact map location is acceptable.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.defaultBehavior: 32 means full precision. Lower values reduce accuracy before reporting.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.summary: User opt-in for including this node location in MQTT map reporting.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.whenToUse: Enable only when the user agrees that the node location may be published through MQTT map systems.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.defaultBehavior: When disabled, map reporting should avoid sending the location even if map reporting is otherwise configured.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.MapReportSetting.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ena.summary: Turns Serial on or off. The Serial module connects external hardware or software through UART pins.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ena.whenToUse: Enable it only when you use serial; disable it to save resources and avoid extra traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ena.defaultBehavior: Disabled is safest when the feature is not installed or not needed.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ena.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ech.summary: Echoes serial input back on the Serial module connection for simple testing and diagnostics.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ech.whenToUse: Use while checking wiring or terminal communication with an external serial device.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ech.defaultBehavior: Disable for normal integrations if echoed data confuses the connected equipment.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ech.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.rxd.summary: rxd selects the hardware line used by Serial. The Serial module connects external hardware or software through UART pins.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.rxd.whenToUse: Set it according to your board or external module wiring.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.rxd.defaultBehavior: Board defaults are safest for built-in hardware; wrong pins can stop the feature or conflict with another function.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.rxd.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.txd.summary: txd selects the hardware line used by Serial. The Serial module connects external hardware or software through UART pins.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.txd.whenToUse: Set it according to your board or external module wiring.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.txd.defaultBehavior: Board defaults are safest for built-in hardware; wrong pins can stop the feature or conflict with another function.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.txd.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.bau.whenToUse: Set it to exactly match the connected GPS, logger, controller, or computer serial setting.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.bau.defaultBehavior: If baud rates do not match, received text will look corrupted or no data will be exchanged.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.tim.summary: timeout controls how often Serial sends, updates, or repeats its data. The Serial module connects external hardware or software through UART pins.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.tim.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.tim.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.tim.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.mod.summary: Selects what the Serial module sends or expects on the UART connection: simple text, protobuf API, NMEA/CalTopo output, logging, or device-specific protocols.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.mod.whenToUse: Choose the mode required by the external system connected to the serial pins.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.mod.defaultBehavior: Wrong mode can send data in a format the external device cannot understand.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.mod.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

TEXTMSG.title: Text messages
TEXTMSG.description: Serial data is treated as mesh text messages.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ove.summary: Lets the Serial module use the platform default console serial port instead of only the configured module pins.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.SerialConfig.ove.whenToUse: Use mainly for output modes such as NMEA or CalTopo when the connected system is on the console serial port.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.NeighborInfoConf.summary: Turns Neighbor Info on or off. Neighbor Info reports which nearby nodes this node can hear.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.NeighborInfoConf.whenToUse: Enable it only when you use neighbor info; disable it to save resources and avoid extra traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.NeighborInfoConf.defaultBehavior: Disabled is safest when the feature is not installed or not needed.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.NeighborInfoConf.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.NeighborInfoConf.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.
