meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.defaultBehavior: Too high a current can waste power or stress the LED module.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.summary: Brightness level for the red color channel of the RGB LED.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.whenToUse: Adjust it to mix the desired color.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.defaultBehavior: Use 0 to turn this color off and 255 for maximum brightness.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.summary: Brightness level for the green color channel of the RGB LED.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.whenToUse: Adjust it to mix the desired color.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.defaultBehavior: Use 0 to turn this color off and 255 for maximum brightness.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.summary: Brightness level for the blue color channel of the RGB LED.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.whenToUse: Adjust it to mix the desired color.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.AmbientLightingC.defaultBehavior: Use 0 to turn this color off and 255 for maximum brightness.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.whenToUse: Enable it only when you use detection sensor; disable it to save resources and avoid extra traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Disabled is safest when the feature is not installed or not needed.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.summary: minimum broadcast secs controls how often Detection Sensor sends, updates, or repeats its data. Detection Sensor watches a GPIO input and sends an alert when the configured trigger occurs.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.summary: Adds a bell character to detection alert messages.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.whenToUse: Use when receiving devices should trigger External Notification behavior for detection alerts.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Disable if detection alerts should remain normal text alerts only.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.summary: Friendly name inserted into detection messages, such as “Motion” for “Motion detected”.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.whenToUse: Set it so users understand which sensor triggered.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Keep it short and clear; long names make alerts harder to read.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.summary: monitor pin selects the hardware line used by Detection Sensor. Detection Sensor watches a GPIO input and sends an alert when the configured trigger occurs.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.whenToUse: Set it according to your board or external module wiring.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Board defaults are safest for built-in hardware; wrong pins can stop the feature or conflict with another function.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Enter the GPIO or hardware pin number from your board documentation. A wrong pin can stop the feature or affect the wrong circuit.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.summary: Chooses the electrical event on the monitored GPIO pin that counts as detection: low level, high level, rising edge, falling edge, or any change.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.whenToUse: Set it to match how the connected sensor signals an event. Motion sensors, switches, and alarms can use different active levels.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Wrong trigger type can cause no alerts or constant false alerts.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

LOGIC_LOW.title: Logic low
LOGIC_LOW.description: Alert while the pin is LOW.

LOGIC_HIGH.title: Logic high
LOGIC_HIGH.description: Alert while the pin is HIGH.

FALLING_EDGE.title: Falling edge
FALLING_EDGE.description: Alert when the pin changes from HIGH to LOW.

RISING_EDGE.title: Rising edge
RISING_EDGE.description: Alert when the pin changes from LOW to HIGH.

EITHER_EDGE_ACTIVE_LOW.title: Either edge, low active
EITHER_EDGE_ACTIVE_LOW.description: Alert on any change; LOW is treated as active.

EITHER_EDGE_ACTIVE_HIGH.title: Either edge, high active
EITHER_EDGE_ACTIVE_HIGH.description: Alert on any change; HIGH is treated as active.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.defaultBehavior: Wrong pull-up setting can cause false triggers or no triggers.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.DetectionSensorC.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.whenToUse: Enable it only when you use paxcounter; disable it to save resources and avoid extra traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.defaultBehavior: Disabled is safest when the feature is not installed or not needed.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.PaxcounterConfig.valueHint: Enter RSSI in dBm, usually a negative number such as -80.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.StatusMessageCon.summary: Text status that this node periodically rebroadcasts.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.StatusMessageCon.whenToUse: Use to show a short human-readable state such as location role, availability, or operational note.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.StatusMessageCon.defaultBehavior: Keep it short and non-sensitive because other mesh users may see it.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.StatusMessageCon.valueHint: Enter text in the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Turns Traffic Management on or off. Traffic Management reduces channel load by dropping duplicates and limiting noisy traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Enable it only when you use traffic management; disable it to save resources and avoid extra traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Disabled is safest when the feature is not installed or not needed.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: position dedup enabled controls how position broadcasts are deduplicated or limited.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use to reduce repeated tracker/location traffic on busy channels.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Too much filtering can make moving nodes look stale.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: position precision bits controls how position broadcasts are deduplicated or limited.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use to reduce repeated tracker/location traffic on busy channels.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Too much filtering can make moving nodes look stale.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: position min interval secs controls how often Traffic Management sends, updates, or repeats its data. Traffic Management reduces channel load by dropping duplicates and limiting noisy traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Allows the node to answer NodeInfo requests from its local cache instead of forcing more network traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use to reduce repeated NodeInfo traffic on busy meshes.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Disable if direct cached responses are not wanted for your deployment.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Minimum hop distance from the requester before this node sends a direct NodeInfo response.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Tune when direct responses should help distant requesters but avoid answering nearby ones unnecessarily.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Too low can create extra responses; too high can make the feature ineffective.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: rate limit enabled controls per-node rate limiting for chatty devices.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use on busy meshes where one node can consume too much airtime.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Too strict limits can block legitimate traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: rate limit window secs controls how often Traffic Management sends, updates, or repeats its data. Traffic Management reduces channel load by dropping duplicates and limiting noisy traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Increase it to reduce battery use and airtime; decrease it only when fresher or more noticeable updates are important.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Default intervals are usually a safe balance between freshness and channel load.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Enter time in seconds. Smaller values update more often and can use more battery and airtime.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: rate limit max packets controls per-node rate limiting for chatty devices.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use on busy meshes where one node can consume too much airtime.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Too strict limits can block legitimate traffic.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Use the format expected by the firmware. If unsure, keep the existing value.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Drops unknown or undecryptable packets after the configured threshold within the rate-limit window.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use on busy meshes to reduce repeated traffic that this node cannot understand.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Too aggressive settings can drop useful packets from misconfigured or newly joined nodes.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Number of unknown packets allowed from a node before dropping starts.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Lower it to protect airtime from noisy unknown traffic; raise it if valid nodes are being dropped too quickly.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: This works with the rate-limit window.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Enter a number in the unit described above. Use 0 only when the description says that 0 means default or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Sets hop_limit to 0 for relayed telemetry broadcasts, while leaving this node own packets unaffected.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use to keep telemetry from being relayed farther across a busy mesh.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Can reduce coverage of telemetry data beyond the first relay.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.summary: Sets hop_limit to 0 for relayed position broadcasts, while leaving this node own packets unaffected.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use to keep position traffic local on a busy mesh.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Can reduce how far position updates propagate.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.whenToUse: Use when router links should keep forwarding budget across infrastructure nodes.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.defaultBehavior: Wrong use can change how far traffic travels through router paths.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TrafficManagemen.valueHint: Only two values are possible: enabled or disabled.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TAKConfig.team.whenToUse: Choose the color that matches the user team in TAK workflows.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TAKConfig.team.defaultBehavior: If left unspecified, firmware uses its default team color.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TAKConfig.team.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TAKConfig.role.summary: TAK member role reported for TAK/ATAK integrations.

meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TAKConfig.role.defaultBehavior: If left unspecified, firmware uses its default team member role.
meshtastic.ModuleConfig.TAKConfig.role.valueHint: Choose one option from the list. The option descriptions explain what each value does.

category.whenToUse: Expand it and change only settings whose purpose you understand.
category.defaultBehavior: If unsure, leave values inside the section unchanged.

boolean.summary: A switch turns a feature on or off.
boolean.whenToUse: Change it when you explicitly want to enable or disable the described feature.
boolean.defaultBehavior: If unsure, keep the current value.

true.title: Enabled
true.description: The feature is active and the device will use the described behavior.

false.title: Disabled
false.description: The feature is not used. This is usually safe when you do not need it.

enum.summary: This setting chooses one mode from a fixed list.
enum.whenToUse: Change it when you know which mode your use case needs.
enum.defaultBehavior: If unsure, keep the current mode.
enum.valueHint: All firmware-supported choices are listed below.

number.summary: A numeric setting defines an interval, threshold, pin, power, or another quantity.
number.whenToUse: Change only if you know the unit and understand what the number affects.
number.defaultBehavior: If unsure, keep the current value.
number.valueHint: Enter a number. Very short intervals can drain battery and use more airtime.

string.summary: A text setting: name, address, key, topic, format, or another string.
string.whenToUse: Change it when you need a specific text, address, or format.
string.defaultBehavior: An empty string often means firmware default behavior.
string.valueHint: Enter text without extra spaces. For addresses and formats, follow the example in the setting description.

bytes.summary: Binary data shown in encoded form.
bytes.whenToUse: Change only when you have the exact key or data value.
bytes.defaultBehavior: A wrong value can break access, encryption, or administrative features.

repeated.summary: A list of values of the same type.
repeated.whenToUse: Add or remove list entries only when you understand what each entry means.
repeated.defaultBehavior: The empty last row is used to add a new value.
repeated.valueHint: Each row in the list is a separate value.
